narrative.overview:
Today's shift is a pass you carry. One near-black card holds everything about the shift (what it is, where it is up to, where the finish line sits, how long you have worked), and one red button docked in thumb reach does the one job. Everything else sits quietly on a white ground in hairline rows and plain words. The world borrows its calm from wallet passes and banking confirmations, and its colour from the club itself: black iron, red frames, white floor.

The system is light and phone-first. Density is low on purpose: big tabular numerals, 15 to 16px text, 44px+ touch targets, one idea per row. The brand appears only in small deliberate places (the red action, the red live dot, the uppercase text wordmark). Problems are never red and never blocks; they are amber notes for a person to check, and the record is always reassured as saved. The same world carries two surfaces: the cleaner's home (one pass, one docked red action) and the manager's dashboard, a calm to-do list of grouped hairline sections where many small decisions are ink, today's roster is the one black pass, and red waits inside a sheet.

The brand layer is **interim**. It approximates World Gym's black/red/white until official assets arrive and is isolated in one block of custom properties so it can be swapped (or neutralised for the portfolio version) without touching components.
keyCharacteristics: One black pass per screen: the Shift Pass with its progress line on the cleaner home, the Today pass on the dashboard.
At most one red action per view or sheet; repeated decisions in a list are ink.
Hairline rows with soft tinted icon discs for status; grouped sections with ink count badges, no card soup.
Geist with tabular numerals everywhere; times and durations are the heroes.
Amber means "a person will look at this"; green means "saved and fine"; red means "do it" or "live".
Motion confirms, never decorates; every movement has a reduced-motion fallback.

rules.name: The Red Means Go Rule
rules.body: Red appears only on the one primary action of a view or sheet and on the live "On shift" dot. Where a list holds many approvals (requests on the dashboard, team swaps on a lead's home), Approve is ink, so red stays one per view and one per sheet. Red is never a problem, error, warning, decline or decoration colour. The shadcn `destructive` token is not part of this system.

rules.name: The Note For Carly Rule
rules.body: Every flag, location problem or failure is amber and never blocks an action. Cleaners read it as "Carly will check it" with reassurance that time is saved; Carly reads the same flag as a neutral fact to check ("Priya · away from the gym"), never an accusation.

rules.name: The Swappable Brand Rule
rules.body: Brand colour lives only in the brand layer (`--brand`, `--brand-press`, `--brand-foreground`, `--pass`, `--pass-foreground`, `--pass-muted`, `--pass-line`, `--pass-zone`). These are the tokens to replace when official World Gym assets arrive; the wordmark text is the asset to replace with the official logo. No component hardcodes a brand hex.

rules.name: The Numbers Lead Rule
rules.body: Times and durations are the largest thing in any block and always tabular. Durations read "43 min", "2h 17m", "3h"; times read "7:00 pm" with one am/pm per range.

rules.name: The Uppercase Is The Wordmark Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracking is reserved for the interim text wordmark. No other label is set in caps.

rules.name: The Only Objects Cast Rule
rules.body: Only pass-like objects (the black pass and upcoming cards) cast shadows. Everything else is flat.

rules.name: The Never Cut Rule
rules.body: Nothing on screen or in an export clips, caps or rounds worked time down. Past the mark the progress line keeps filling and the stat reads "Over"; hours totals and the CSV use exact corrected minutes, with H:MM and decimal hours derived from them and decimals rounded up.

rules.name: The One Pass Rule
rules.body: One black pass per screen. Other information goes in rows, sections or white cards, never a second black card.

rules.name: The Settle In Place Rule
rules.body: A decision in a list is made in the row, waits 5 seconds with Undo, then settles and folds away. It is never re-offered and never sent to another screen to confirm.

dos: **Do** keep Club Red to the single primary action of a view or sheet and the 7px live dot.
**Do** make Approve ink wherever a list holds more than one decision.
**Do** use Check Amber for every flag; tell cleaners "Carly will check it" and that the time is saved, and show Carly a neutral fact.
